title: internal-author-onramp-for-sdk-quickstarts-draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a fast onramp for people writing SDK quickstarts and short how-tos for developer-facing teams. It aims to reduce iteration time by giving a compact template, telemetry hooks to add, common pitfalls, and a short checklist for ship readiness.

Audience:
- Docs/Content engineers creating new SDK quickstarts
- SDK engineers pairing on samples
- Solutions folks preparing demo flows

Why this exists (notes to self):
- We keep seeing inconsistent quickstarts (too long, missing auth, no failover guidance).
- Authors often forget telemetry / eval prompts that let Product measure regressions.
- Goal: make a 3-min demo + 15-min deeper guide that are both easy to maintain.

Minimum deliverables for a new SDK quickstart (3 artifacts):
1) One-page TL;DR (3-min): purpose, prerequisites, copy-paste auth snippet, 2 API calls that show success and error handling.
2) Expanded guide (15-min): sample app flow, edge cases, links to SDK reference.
3) Tiny integration test: single CI job that runs the 3-min script against staging tokens.

Template: TL;DR (copyable)
- Title (one line)
- Use-case blurb (1-2 sentences)
- Prereqs: node/Python version, package name, env var name for API key
- Auth snippet (copy/paste) + how to set a staging key (link)
- Minimal sample: 6-10 lines, annotated
- Expected output example (plaintext)
- Quick troubleshooting (2 bullets)

Template: 15-min guide (sections)
- Background + when to use this SDK surface
- Step-by-step app build (with file names)
- Error patterns and recovery: rate limit retry policy examples, streaming cancellation
- Observability checklist: what to log and why
- Security notes: KMS/HSM usage, local key handling

Telemetry & CI hooks (must-add):
- SDK quickstart should emit 3 telemetry events to staging: start_quickstart, success_quickstart, quickstart_error with error_code. Use the SDK built-in telemetry client.
- Add a tiny smoke CI: runs the TL;DR script, asserts exit 0 and expected keys in stdout. Attach artifacts to PR.
- Link a minimal eval prompt for output-quality monitoring (prompt id -> evaluations service).

Common author pitfalls (copy into PR checklist):
- Missing exact versions (use locked examples).
- Sample uses prod keys — explicitly instruct to use staging and how to get one.
- Long-winded examples: split into TL;DR + deep dive.
- No failover guidance for Hosted -> Dedicated variants; include a short note on route fallbacks.

Quick failure-mode snippets (for the 15-min guide):
- Rate limit: exponential backoff pseudo-code (3 retries, jitter)
- Streaming timeouts: how to cancel and resume with token prefix caching
- Large responses: recommend pagination/stream-chunking and memory budgets

Ship checklist (for PR description):
- [ ] TL;DR present and under 200 words
- [ ] Copyable auth snippet with env var name matching internal convention (REDWOOD_API_KEY_STAGE)
- [ ] CI smoke job added to docs-smoke pipeline
- [ ] Telemetry events instrumented and linked to ENG-1242
- [ ] Linked SDK reference and model catalog entry
- [ ] Accessibility: code blocks keyboard-focusable and alt text on images
- [ ] Reviewer: eng-developer-experience + SDK owner

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should templates include a sample that exercises the Optimize batching recommendation? (Priya to decide)
- Where to store canonical staging tokens for internal demos? (SRE ops runbook link needed)
- Quickstart lint rules: add a docs-linter rule to enforce telemetry events? (tracked in ENG-1361)

Notes for pairing sessions:
- 30m session: author + SDK engineer to produce TL;DR and CI smoke.
- 60m session: finish 15-min guide, add telemetry, open PR.

Slack snippets (for PR description):
- Title: [docs] sdk quickstart: {sdk} - {short use}
- Body: why, checklist link (this doc), smoke CI link, reviewer suggestions

References and links (internal):
- Writer's style guide: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/WRITER/Style+guide
- Docs repo template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/tree/main/templates/quickstart
- Demo token request: #sre-demo-keys on Slack

Endnotes: keep this doc short and iterated in PR; it should live next to other templates in the docs repo. Mark as draft until Priya signs off on telemetry requirements.

-- Asha
